tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

No, not everything. The code the plan builds on all exists in the JusPrin, tsd-enterprise and obico-server checkouts. But a few answers from you are needed before it can run end to end, and most of those are already listed in the plan's section 6. A lot of the code can still be written now with placeholders.

**What I checked**
- OrcaSlicer's `OAuthJob`, `HttpServer` and `OAuthDialog` are in this checkout. `OAuthParams` has a `verification_code` field, and `OAuthJob` sends it as `code_verifier` when it exchanges the code for a token. So PKCE (the browser sign-in with a code challenge) is supported.
- JusPrin's `ProviderProfile.hpp` has the OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic rows, and `ResponsesCodec`, `ModelCatalog` and `ProviderAgent` exist.
- obico-server (master `eb0f29c`, the commit the tsd-enterprise checkout has) has django-oauth-toolkit 2.3.0, a 100-year token lifetime, `PKCE_REQUIRED: False`, `responses_transport.py`, and `consume_credit_for_pipeline(user_id)`.
- tsd-enterprise has `web_ent/jusprin/urls.py` with no `v2/` route yet, so the gateway would be all new files.

**What only you can give me**
1. **The OAuth application's `client_id`.** Someone creates it in the oauth2 admin with the fixed loopback redirect port, and the port has to be picked first. A local obico-server is enough for development, but I haven't checked that one runs here.
2. **The first model alias.** Which upstream provider, model and effort `jusprin-1` maps to, and the env variable names for the keys. Without them the gateway can only run against a fake upstream.
3. **Hosts:** production and staging, and whether there is a China host.
4. **Pricing, the 402 message, and the catalog labels and effort names.** These can stay placeholders while I code.
5. **Migration decisions:** whether to import the v1 data directory, whether to import the v1 token, and whether v2 keeps v1's installer identity. They only affect the migration part, not sign-in or the gateway.
6. **The leaked key.** The plan says `dotenv.example` in tsd-enterprise holds what looks like a live OpenAI key. Only you can rotate it, and it should be done before anything else.

**Two things the plan gets slightly wrong**
- The plan calls the new `CloudSignIn` service "GUI-free". But `OAuthJob` is an OrcaSlicer `Job`: it needs a job worker to run on, and it reports its result through a wx event. It can still be used without editing any OrcaSlicer file, but the service is not as GUI-free as `ProviderKeySetup`.
- The PKCE helpers (`generate_verification_code`, `sha256b64`) are `static` functions inside `SimplyPrint.cpp`, so they can't be called from JusPrin code. JusPrin needs its own copy of about ten lines.

**What I can build now, with placeholders**
- The client:
  - the `jusprin` provider row
  - the sign-in service
  - the new bridge messages
  - the account row on the page
  - the catalog branch for alias ids
  - mapping 402 to `quota_exhausted`
  - tests
- The gateway, tested against a fake upstream:
  - aliases
  - streaming with the model name rewritten
  - one credit charge per turn
  - upstream 401 sent to the client as 502
  - the models endpoint

<cross-session-message from="local_5e15ee7b-2a48-4e3b-935a-3dfd37ce96ff" name="Cloud provider plan review">
Kenneth says: start implementing the JusPrin Cloud provider plan (~/Downloads/cloud-provider-plan.md). He settled every open question in a side session; here are the decisions, which override the plan where they differ.

1. Model alias: id "slicer-1", label "Slicer 1" (not "jusprin-1"). Effort names shown to people: "Fast" (maps to low) and "Thorough" (maps to high), unless he says otherwise.
2. Upstream: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) first. It costs about the same as GPT-5.4 or less ($2/$10 per MTok vs about $2.50/$15).
3. Both formats, so prod can switch between Anthropic and OpenAI and A/B test them. This replaces plan decision 1 (Responses only):
   - The gateway has two passthrough endpoints, /ent/jusprin/v2/responses (OpenAI upstream) and /ent/jusprin/v2/messages (Anthropic upstream). Neither translates formats. Each swaps the alias for the upstream model, maps effort, replaces upstream errors with generic ones (upstream 401 goes out as 502), and charges credits per turn as the plan says.
   - Each alias in GET /v2/models carries "format": "anthropic" | "responses". The client picks AnthropicCodec or ResponsesCodec, and the endpoint, from that field instead of from the provider row.
   - A/B assignment happens on the server: the gateway config decides per person what "slicer-1" maps to.
   - Each chat is fixed to the backend of its first request for its whole life. New chats pick up a changed assignment.
   - Log the backend and the person's group per turn to Langfuse.
   - Kenneth accepted that the format field reveals the vendor family to someone inspecting their own traffic.
4. OAuth: create a NEW application for v2 (authorization code + PKCE, loopback redirect). Do NOT reuse the v1 "JusPrin" client id: v1 uses the implicit grant (response_type=token), and django-oauth-toolkit allows one grant type per application. For development, create it yourself on a local obico-server. Production comes later and Kenneth will handle it. Check how the "JusPrin" app record gets created for self-hosted servers (a migration?) and do the same for v2.
5. Migration: import the v1 token (sign the person in silently, with no browser round trip) and import v1's data directory (printers, presets, print-host connections, preferences) on first launch.
6. Onboarding mockup approved. Three boards are on the JusPrin v2 canvas, on the onboarding page, in the row "When JusPrin v1 is on this computer": V1-01 imported, V1-02 partly imported, V1-03 sign-in expired. The screen is shown after 00 Welcome and replaces 01–09. The OrcaSlicer import becomes a small link.
7. The leaked key in tsd-enterprise's dotenv.example: Kenneth will not rotate it. Leave it.
8. Implementation notes found while checking the plan:
   - OrcaSlicer's OAuthJob is a Job: it needs a worker and reports through a wx event, so CloudSignIn is not fully GUI-free.
   - The PKCE helpers in SimplyPrint.cpp are static, so JusPrin needs its own copy (about 10 lines).
   - OAuthJob::parse_token_response requires a refresh_token in the token response.

Hosts, pricing and quota numbers, and Langfuse retention stay placeholders. Nothing else is needed from Kenneth before starting.
</cross-session-message>

=== agent-setup-one-flow-decisions.md
---
name: agent-setup-one-flow-decisions
description: 2026-10-23 Kenneth decided Preferences › Agent is the one Agent setup flow for every entry point (first time too); surfaces show their own not-set-up state, resume after the window closes, nothing auto-sent; cancel changes nothing.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided 2026-10-23 in a design session; the full document is the untracked `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md` in
the main checkout root (never committed). Context: JusPrin's own Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui as
641c17f13e (modal over any screen, Agent section draws the same key/tool rows as setup, shell reloads the docked
agent on close if `jusprin_agent` changed).

Kenneth's decisions:
1. Preferences › Agent is the one setup flow, first time included. The in-pane chooser, the printer panel's
   in-body chooser, the print-issue MessageDialog ("Set up now / Not now"), `open_agent_setup`/`request_setup`
   and `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` are to go. The first-run setup boards on the canvas page "Agent setup &
   Preferences" are history.
2. No separate question. Each surface shows its own not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences ›
   Agent: the print-issue bubble draws one button "Set up the agent…" (Kenneth chose "agent" over "assistant") instead of Ask AI / Resolve with AI;
   the pane and printer panel keep their "No agent connected" offer and setup bar; calibration's board-3
   Confirmation adds one sentence and its primary button reads "Set up the agent…".
3. When the window closes with an agent, the surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent for the
   person (bubble shows its two buttons; confirmation's button becomes "Start test"; panel greeting continues).
4. Cancel changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was; the printer panel is never closed
   on the person's behalf.
5. The pane keeps its own entry (offer, setup bar, chat list row), each opening Preferences › Agent.

**Why:** three different answers to "needs the agent, none set up" existed and calibration would add a fourth;
Kenneth: "On the homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"
The Agent pane does not exist on Home (force-collapsed in `on_page_changed`), so only a window over Home works.

**How to apply:** any new entry point that needs the Agent follows rule 2 to 4; never add a chooser inside a
pane or a MessageDialog. Implementation detail noted: the printer panel builds its runtime at `open()` and must
reload it after Preferences closes. Related: [[calibration-design-decisions]], [[agent-setup-api-key-path]],
[[api-key-saved-state]], [[use-orca-messagedialog]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].

Canvas (2026-10-23): board "Agent setup · one door" on the "Agent setup & Preferences" page and board 3b on "Calibration · Printer & Filament" draw these states; builder `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_no_agent_boards.py`. With no provider set up, the composer's model picker shows the raw id "gpt-5.4-mini" (default provider openai, empty catalogue) and no thinking picker; Kenneth asked for it drawn.
=== agent-setup-api-key-path.md
---
name: agent-setup-api-key-path
description: "JusPrin Agent setup, API-key route — verification-is-construction design, privacy rule for the probe, and the routes deliberately left unbuilt."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb922e6b-d324-4167-adb6-c08ea83efb8f
  modified: 2026-09-14T16:29:41.120Z
---

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"
(needs a JusPrin MCP server that may not exist, and a download source to
confirm before writing code that fetches a binary).

Testing this path: the shell harness points `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` at a
closed local port so the real host, page, and HTTP transport are exercised
without an external service — that covers the failure path only. For a real
key, `--manual-unconfigured` (see [[jusprin-shell-manual-harness]]). The key now lives in the harness's AppConfig, so it does not survive runs;
an old `JusPrin Agent OpenAI` Keychain entry is ignored.
=== api-key-saved-state.md
---
name: api-key-saved-state
description: "2026-10-21 saved-key display on the \"Your own API key\" screen, committed 2d19270c49 on jusprin-newui, pushed 2026-10-21; how \"rejected\" is decided."
metadata:

  type: project
  originSessionId: 59133fd8-af56-4958-bb71-9b4812c085b8
  modified: 2026-10-21T14:27:12.176Z
---

Built from the canvas board "api-key-field · saved vs empty · proposal" (Agent Setup · Empty State page). Committed 2026-10-21 as 2d19270c49 on jusprin-newui (fast-forward from f073fdba96), pushed the same day.

- Capability `saved_keys`: host→page `setup_keys {keys:[{provider,hint,rejected}]}`, page→host `setup_remove_key {provider}`. Hint = `api_key_hint()` in AgentSetup.cpp: a fixed per-provider prefix table + "…" + last 4, tail hidden unless ≥8 chars stay hidden.
- Remove: AppConfig item erased and saved at once; if it was the recorded `provider`, that moves to the first provider still holding a key; host rebuilds the agent from the model source (or goes Unavailable when none left).
- **"Rejected" is my interpretation, not Kenneth's:** the board shows a check of the saved key, but nothing checks a saved key today. I chose: a chat turn whose provider answers `invalid_credentials` (401/403) marks that provider's key rejected, in memory, keyed by hint so a replaced key clears it. No auto-probe on screen open (would cost a live call each open). The printer-panel host (no model source) cannot attribute a refusal and never marks one.
- Key field = Field/Secret (Kenneth, 2026-10-21): `--field-height` 26, `--field-padding-x` 8, value in code, placeholder body / text-secondary as Field/Text draws it; actions are Button/Link. Board rebuilt to match by `figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_key_states.py` (board now 962 tall, canvas version 44).

Related: [[agent-setup-api-key-path]], [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]], [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]].

Branch `claude/composer-redesign` (worktree `JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`,
on top of `claude/design-token-sync` 76105af26c), uncommitted as of 2026-10-20:
composer redesign, native file picker (`pick_attachment`), and per-chat
provider/model/thinking pickers (`model_choice` capability: `set_chat_model`,
`model_catalog`, `chat_model`).

Design that matters:
- Kenneth's goal: switch provider, model and thinking level at any point in
  a chat, like ChatGPT/claude.ai. Earlier turns replay provider-neutrally (no
  thinking blocks cross turns), so a switch needs no history translation.
- Choice stored per chat as `chatModel` in the project's Agent document;
  absent = default provider's default model.
- An agent handed to the host (constructor, setup, harness mock) counts as
  the default choice's agent. Rebuilding it on the first turn stalled the
  full harness once; host test "a chat's model choice decides the agent each
  turn runs on" guards this.
- Lists: Anthropic GET /v1/models (capabilities → effort levels, adaptive
  only); OpenRouter /api/v1/models?supported_parameters=tools (`reasoning`
  object); OpenAI /v1/models has no capability data, so ModelCatalog.cpp
  guesses (gpt-5*/o* get low/medium/high).

**Live smoke, 2026-10-20 (Kenneth approved using the OpenAI key stored in
~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf for that batch only):**
`agent_live_tests "[models][live]"` passed for OpenAI: 76 models listed,
a one-word reply on gpt-5.4-nano at effort low, then gpt-5.4-mini. Anthropic
and OpenRouter have no stored key and are live-untested. Ask before any
further live run. Open design question: OpenRouter's tool-capable list
is hundreds long (menu scrolls; search or curation undecided).

(Composer measures; .composer-choices--narrow hides "Thinking:"), model-menu search
above 12 models (component.fieldSearch token), and the WebKit menu-click fix

Merged 2026-10-20 into local jusprin-newui as 1ca65bb087 (unpushed): two commits,

backup/composer-redesign-before-squash.

=== jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact.md
---
name: jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact
description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:50:06.847Z
---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

=== jusprin-worktree-build.md
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
=== subagent-worktrees-create-manually.md
---
name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
=== never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree.md
---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

=== agent-setup-api-key-path.md
---
name: agent-setup-api-key-path
description: "JusPrin Agent setup, API-key route — verification-is-construction design, privacy rule for the probe, and the routes deliberately left unbuilt."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb922e6b-d324-4167-adb6-c08ea83efb8f
  modified: 2026-09-14T16:29:41.120Z
---

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"
(needs a JusPrin MCP server that may not exist, and a download source to
confirm before writing code that fetches a binary).

Testing this path: the shell harness points `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` at a
closed local port so the real host, page, and HTTP transport are exercised
without an external service — that covers the failure path only. For a real
key, `--manual-unconfigured` (see [[jusprin-shell-manual-harness]]). The key now lives in the harness's AppConfig, so it does not survive runs;
an old `JusPrin Agent OpenAI` Keychain entry is ignored.

=== jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact.md
---
name: jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact
description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:50:06.847Z
---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools
sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card
were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the
canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list +
__EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written
`components/<Name>/preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg,
README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call.
=== jusprin-worktree-build.md
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
=== subagent-worktrees-create-manually.md
---
name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].
=== never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree.md
---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

Decided 2026-10-23 in a design session; the full document is the untracked `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md` in
the main checkout root (never committed). Context: JusPrin's own Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui as
641c17f13e (modal over any screen, Agent section draws the same key/tool rows as setup, shell reloads the docked
agent on close if `jusprin_agent` changed).

Kenneth's decisions:
1. Preferences › Agent is the one setup flow, first time included. The in-pane chooser, the printer panel's
   in-body chooser, the print-issue MessageDialog ("Set up now / Not now"), `open_agent_setup`/`request_setup`
   and `AgentPageMode::EmbeddedSetup` are to go. The first-run setup boards on the canvas page "Agent setup &
   Preferences" are history.
2. No separate question. Each surface shows its own not-set-up state with one action that opens Preferences ›
   Agent: the print-issue bubble draws one button "Set up the agent…" (Kenneth chose "agent" over "assistant") instead of Ask AI / Resolve with AI;
   the pane and printer panel keep their "No agent connected" offer and setup bar; calibration's board-3
   Confirmation adds one sentence and its primary button reads "Set up the agent…".
3. When the window closes with an agent, the surface resumes with the agent live; nothing is sent for the
   person (bubble shows its two buttons; confirmation's button becomes "Start test"; panel greeting continues).
4. Cancel changes nothing underneath; the pending choice stays where it was; the printer panel is never closed
   on the person's behalf.
5. The pane keeps its own entry (offer, setup bar, chat list row), each opening Preferences › Agent.

**Why:** three different answers to "needs the agent, none set up" existed and calibration would add a fourth;
Kenneth: "On the homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"
The Agent pane does not exist on Home (force-collapsed in `on_page_changed`), so only a window over Home works.

**How to apply:** any new entry point that needs the Agent follows rule 2 to 4; never add a chooser inside a
pane or a MessageDialog. Implementation detail noted: the printer panel builds its runtime at `open()` and must

=== agent-setup-api-key-path.md
---
name: agent-setup-api-key-path
description: "JusPrin Agent setup, API-key route — verification-is-construction design, privacy rule for the probe, and the routes deliberately left unbuilt."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb922e6b-d324-4167-adb6-c08ea83efb8f
  modified: 2026-09-14T16:29:41.120Z
---

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design came from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames); since 2026-10-20 the up-to-date version of that page is the
"Agent Setup · Empty State" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
